searches.purpose: Locate origin, primary bibliography, methods, independent critique, empirical outcomes, current continuation, safety and cultural materials while separating White-Epston narrative therapy from narrative exposure therapy, narrative medicine and generic storytelling interventions

items.title: Histories
items.rights_note: Dulwich Centre account of Michael White, David Epston and other contributors; participant history, not independent historiography.

items.title: Narrative Means to Therapeutic Ends
items.rights_note: Open Library bibliographic page for the 1990 first edition; borrow/preview status does not authorize caching or treating the book body as read.

items.title: What is Narrative Therapy?
items.rights_note: Authorized public extract presenting collaboration, externalization, stories, thin description and re-authoring; practitioner exposition rather than independent validation.

items.title: Review of Narrative Therapy: Research and Utility
items.rights_note: ERIC abstract and bibliographic record for an early independent research review; article body is not open here and is not counted as a full-text read.

items.title: Psychotherapy focusing on dialogical and narrative perspectives: a systematic review from qualitative and mixed-methods studies
items.rights_note: Open systematic review of dialogical and narrative psychotherapies; its broader combined scope must not be treated as evidence for White-Epston narrative therapy alone.

items.title: A systematic review of narrative therapy treatment outcomes for eating disorders
items.rights_note: Open condition-specific review; limited standardized outcome evidence and predominance of case material must remain explicit and cannot establish general efficacy.

items.title: About narrative approaches
items.rights_note: Current Dulwich Centre self-description; evidence of institutional continuation and scope only, not independent efficacy support.

items.title: The stories we need to tell: Using online outsider-witness processes and digital storytelling in a remote Australian Aboriginal community
items.rights_note: Directly relevant community-collaborative report with Aboriginal co-authorship and cultural guidance, but the PDF states that no part may be stored or transmitted without permission.
items.exclusion_reason: Do not retrieve or cache a document whose embedded rights statement expressly restricts storage and transmission; seek an openly licensed community-led alternative.

items.title: Efficacy and cultural adaptations of narrative exposure therapy for trauma-related outcomes in refugees and asylum-seekers
items.rights_note: Open cultural-adaptation review of Narrative Exposure Therapy (NET), a distinct trauma-focused intervention rather than White-Epston narrative therapy.
items.exclusion_reason: Name overlap is insufficient: Narrative Exposure Therapy is a distinct treatment and cannot fill narrative therapy's cultural-context slot.
